nodes.label: Prava Account
nodes.rationale: No standalone wallet object: the account holds enrolled cards and addresses, and all of an owner's agents draw on the same cards with no per-agent permissions.

nodes.label: Agent Linking
nodes.rationale: All-or-nothing active/revoked state, not a permissions matrix; revoking cuts off access immediately.

nodes.label: Checkout Quota
nodes.rationale: Lifetime checkout count enforced by Prava at application level, consumed as agents buy.

nodes.label: Per-Merchant Amount Limits
nodes.rationale: Enforced by the card network (Visa) when a card is enrolled for agentic commerce; quota/concurrency are Prava application-level, merchant/amount locking is network-level.

nodes.label: Card Enrollment & Tokenization
nodes.rationale: Raw card never touches the app or agent: collected via collectPAN or hosted page, then tokenized into a secure stand-in.

nodes.label: Checkout Sequence
nodes.rationale: Human-facing verification (passkey/device binding and issuer OTP) lives inside step 2 card entry and is invisible in the API surface — a first-time integrator budgets time for it.

nodes.label: Device Binding
nodes.rationale: Passkeys are bound per browser/device, so a new browser repeats OTP then passkey registration; a security property, not a bug. Verification runs on the card network's own hosted page so approval is verifiable rather than claimed.

nodes.label: Issuer OTP
nodes.rationale: 3-D Secure style step-up, first step on a new device; sandbox test code 456789.

nodes.label: Passkey (WebAuthn/FIDO)
nodes.rationale: Always the final gate before credentials are issued; the signed passkey proves the cardholder approved this transaction. No fallback — WebAuthn is required.

nodes.label: Browser Harness
nodes.rationale: Checkout automation that confirms the true final total on the live merchant checkout before paying with the one-time token.

nodes.label: Prava API Key Types
nodes.rationale: Publishable key (pk_*) lives in the frontend; secret key (sk_*) backend only; session token authenticates in-session operations.

nodes.label: Guardrails (concept)
nodes.rationale: Rule-based controls enforced at four layers (owner account, mandate, session, authentication) so AI agents cannot exceed authorized scope.

nodes.label: Defense in Depth
nodes.rationale: Owner controls → user passkey → mandate (amount-scoped) → session (time-scoped) → one-time credential; every layer must pass so there is no single point of failure. Amount is enforced at the card-network level through the tokenized credential.

nodes.label: Session-Level Controls
nodes.rationale: Sessions are scoped to a merchant/order, expire and cannot be reused; idempotency rejects duplicate transactions.

nodes.label: Authentication Controls
nodes.rationale: Passkey required for every intent mutation; device binding per browser; no WebAuthn fallback by design.

nodes.label: Prava Payment Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Prava keeps the real card, spending rules, and final authorization out of the caller's hands: propose purchase → secure card entry → owner's rules applied → one-time credential → checkout completes.

nodes.label: Safe by Design
nodes.rationale: No raw card exposure (tokenized), credentials scoped to one purchase, guardrails enforced by Prava not the caller, and Prava declines to guess on uncertain outcomes rather than risk a silent double-charge.

nodes.label: Three Integration Paths
nodes.rationale: Embedded (SDK in your app), Hosted (backend redirect), Agent (AI agent via MCP or CLI) — same lifecycle powers all three.

nodes.label: Mandate (concept)
nodes.rationale: Standing spending authorization: owner approves once with a passkey, agent charges later within caps without re-approval. One-time mandates valid up to 7 days; recurring run multi-cycle. Scheduled subscriptions (Prava auto-charge) are coming next.

nodes.label: Mandate Setup Phase
nodes.rationale: Only the human step: created through a session carrying a mandate_setup block (no standalone create endpoint); owner confirms with passkey — that single approval is the standing consent.

nodes.label: Mandate Charge Phase
nodes.rationale: Agent mints fresh single-use credentials with no new passkey, as many times as caps allow; deliberately not exposed over MCP (CLI and REST only).

nodes.label: Mandate Lifecycle Statuses
nodes.rationale: pending → active → paused/consumed/cancelled/expired; illegal transitions refused with 409 MANDATE_INVALID_TRANSITION.

nodes.label: Mandate Guardrails
nodes.rationale: A mandate is itself a guardrail: amount cap enforced at network level, merchant scope listed/any (403 MANDATE_MERCHANT_NOT_ALLOWED), frequency one_time or recurring, validity window.

nodes.label: Payment Lifecycle (3 calls + hand-off)
nodes.rationale: From your side a payment is exactly three API calls and one hand-off: create session → card entry → payment result → checkout with token → report status. Everything in the middle is Prava's, no API call from you.

nodes.label: Session (concept)
nodes.rationale: Starting point created server-to-server with a secret key; bundles customer identity, order details, merchant context; returns session_token and iframe_url; expires after 15 minutes.

nodes.label: Transaction (concept)
nodes.rationale: Single payment attempt within a session (addCard or savedCard); deduplicated by a deterministic idempotency key derived from order, flow type, and card fingerprint so retries cannot double-charge.

nodes.label: Mandate (payments)
nodes.rationale: Card-network-level spending permission registered after passkey auth: merchant, amount threshold, frequency, effective duration (default 15 min); line items apply at mandate level, not per line item.

nodes.label: Payment Token (concept)
nodes.rationale: Virtual PAN + expiry + CVV generated against an active mandate: single-use, merchant-locked, amount-scoped, short-lived; enforced at the network level and by Prava.

nodes.label: Settlement & Refunds
nodes.rationale: Settlement follows standard card network flows; refunds via API; disputes routed per settlement agreement. Shopify app integration needs Prava's help — everything else is self-serve.

nodes.label: Add Payments to Your AI App (doc)
AI App Payment Integration Tutorial
nodes.rationale: One backend endpoint creates sessions, one frontend surface collects the card, one callback reads result and reports outcome; secret key never leaves the server.

nodes.label: KYB Verification
nodes.rationale: SDK/API integrators get business-verified when switching to production; sandbox needs none of it — build and test first, verify at go-live.

nodes.label: KYC via Card Verification
nodes.rationale: MCP/CLI users get identity verification inherited from their card (issuer OTP) plus passkey approval — your bank already verified you; Prava builds on that.

nodes.label: Prava Legal Status
nodes.rationale: Prava is not a bank, card issuer, acquirer, processor, money transmitter, stored value provider, or deposit-taking institution — a technology service provider for agentic commerce; processing/settlement handled by card networks, banks, and licensed processors; Prava never holds money.

nodes.label: PCI DSS & Skyflow Vaulting
nodes.rationale: PCI DSS Level 2 / SAQ-D compliance with Skyflow (PCI DSS Level 1 vault provider) for card vaulting; no raw card numbers or CVV in application databases.

nodes.label: Go-Live Checklist
nodes.rationale: Keys are environment-bound: sk_test_* against production host fails with AUTH_1001; report every outcome including DECLINED; handle 15-min session expiry; log X-Response-ID for support tracing; production enablement needs Prava's help.

nodes.label: REST Hosted Flow
nodes.rationale: Full payment with nothing but cURL: hosted card entry, redirect to callback_url, poll payment-result, use token + dynamic_cvv at merchant, report APPROVED/DECLINED.

nodes.label: Next.js Breaking Changes Warning
nodes.rationale: This version of Next.js has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may differ from training data; read the relevant guide in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing any code.

nodes.label: Meter Dashboard App
nodes.rationale: Next.js project bootstrapped with create-next-app; edit app/page.tsx with hot reload; uses next/font to load the Geist font family; run with npm run dev.

nodes.label: Linq Partner API
nodes.rationale: RESTful API at https://api.linqapp.com/api/partner/v3 providing programmatic access to iMessage, RCS, and SMS; messages sent through Apple's iMessage protocol using real devices.

nodes.label: Linq Bearer Token Auth
nodes.rationale: Bearer token provisioned by a Linq representative; token determines which phone numbers you can send from.

nodes.label: E.164 Handle Format
nodes.rationale: Phone numbers must be E.164 (+12223334444); no spaces, dashes, or parentheses; email addresses standard format.

nodes.label: Linq LLM-Friendly Docs
nodes.rationale: llms-full.txt is the complete documentation in one file; llms.txt is a concise index — feed straight to an LLM or coding agent.

nodes.label: Linq OpenAPI Canonical Spec
nodes.rationale: The machine-readable OpenAPI spec at https://cdn.linqapp.com/openapi/linq-api-v3.yaml is the canonical definition of every endpoint, request body, response shape, and webhook event.

nodes.label: Chat (Linq)
nodes.rationale: Conversation thread with one or more participants; created with at least one recipient handle; keyed on the from line plus the exact set of to handles.

nodes.label: Message (Linq)
nodes.rationale: Individual communication within a chat thread: text, media attachments, rich link previews, effects, reactions; supports delivery status, read receipts, editing; message carries either parts or a single action, never both.

nodes.label: Attachment (Linq)
nodes.rationale: Files sent with messages; URL-based up to 10MB, pre-upload via attachment_id up to 100MB; bound to the partner account that created it (404 for others' ids); served from cdn.linqapp.com.

nodes.label: Agentcard
nodes.rationale: Let an agent pay on a customer's behalf with a single-use virtual card: connect a customer once, then create a payment — a virtual card is minted scoped to that purchase and handed back for checkout.

nodes.label: Linq Payments (iMessage)
nodes.rationale: Request payment over iMessage with Apple Pay; funds settle directly to your own Stripe account (Stripe Connect Standard, direct charges) — you are merchant of record, Linq is never in the funds flow; refunds/disputes are yours by design; subscriptions: Linq handles first payment, your Stripe account handles the rest.

nodes.label: Ephemeral Privacy Tier
nodes.rationale: For regulated or high-sensitivity conversations: fixed 24-hour message retention / 1-day attachment backstop, permanent deletion after window, no deletion webhook, no expiry timestamp exposed — your app must be the system of record.

nodes.label: W3C Trace Context
nodes.rationale: OpenTelemetry distributed tracing; every response carries X-Trace-ID; server-generated trace context replaces client traceparent per W3C security recommendations for public API trust boundaries.

nodes.label: Chat Health
nodes.rationale: Health buckets HEALTHY/AT_RISK/CRITICAL/OPTED_OUT; many AT_RISK chats on a line increase flagging risk; OPTED_OUT is terminal (STOP/UNSUBSCRIBE keywords) and suppressing sends is your responsibility — Linq surfaces but does not block.

nodes.label: Chat Reuse Keying
nodes.rationale: Chats are keyed on from line plus exact set of to handles — repeating a create returns the existing chat instead of a second conversation; named group chats and changed participant sets produce new chats.

nodes.label: First-Message Link Restriction
nodes.rationale: To protect sender deliverability, the first outbound message of a new chat cannot be a link part or contain a URL (rejected with 400/1005); follow-up messages are exempt.

nodes.label: Message Effects
nodes.rationale: Screen effects (confetti, fireworks, lasers...) and bubble effects (slam, loud, gentle, invisible); only one effect type per message.

nodes.label: Text Decorations
nodes.rationale: Character-range styling (bold/italic/strikethrough/underline) and animations (big, shake, explode...) on text parts; iMessage only — not applied for SMS/RCS; measured in UTF-16 code units; animations must not overlap.

nodes.label: From-Number Auto-Selection
nodes.rationale: POST /v3/messages fuses create-chat and send-message behind a message-centric resource: reuse an existing chat on a healthy line, else new chat on best available line; returns from_selection reason.

nodes.label: Line Failover
nodes.rationale: If existing chats sit only on flagged lines, a new chat is created on a fresh best line and the flagged chat abandoned (failover_flagged); continuation_message replaces the message on that branch; exclusion never abandons a live chat.

nodes.label: Prava SDK (@prava-sdk/core)
nodes.rationale: Lightweight browser library for securely collecting a card: mounts a PCI-compliant iframe and hands back a safe result; raw card number never touches your page, JavaScript, or servers; exposes exactly two methods.

nodes.label: collectPAN
nodes.rationale: Mounts the secure iframe, collects the card, resolves with CollectPANResult (enrollmentId, last4, brand, expMonth, expYear); destroy() tears down iframe and listeners on unmount.

nodes.label: Embedded Mode
nodes.rationale: Prava's card UI runs inside your app via the SDK; set integration_type 'embedding'; result arrives in-app via onSuccess callback.

nodes.label: Hosted Mode
nodes.rationale: Redirect the cardholder to a Prava-hosted page (integration_type 'full_checkout' default) with a callback_url; no SDK; both modes share the same session and iframe_url; iframe_url must be used verbatim.
